cost_model_finding.implication: The P=2 search cost was underestimated at the top of its own priced range. The DEPTH operator dominates at ~32 min per expansion, and P=2 doubles the number of expansions rather than sharing them. Any future attempt needs a repriced allowance derived from the measured 32.3 min DEPTH figure, not from the Phase-A P=1 extrapolation — and that is a reviewer decision, not an adjustment to make quietly.

bottleneck_analysis._basis: Reconstructed from the driver log, which is all that survives: the search journal never came home. The telemetry added in the 2026-08-27 pass measures these directly on the next run instead of inferring them.
bottleneck_analysis.remainder_contents: materialization, canonical reload, validation, state evaluation, statistics collection, and the operators that log no per-candidate line (width, ffn, attention). The split among these was NOT measurable from the log; it is what the new per-expansion telemetry records.
bottleneck_analysis.why_depth_dominates: the intact reference ran in `recomputed` mode, so each of 260 candidates per expansion paid a full reference forward on top of its ablated forward — about 2x the forward work for the whole expansion, twelve expansions over.
bottleneck_analysis.gpu_idleness: observed but not quantified. `distortion(...).as_dict()` materializes Python floats once per item per candidate — 260 x 67 = 17,420 host synchronizations per expansion — which is the most likely source. Deferred item 3 below.
